chunks: Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام: “Indeed, Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام ruled concerning
the tooth of a child, if he has not yet shed it, that it is compensated with one camel.”

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: child; indicating the ruling concerns a minor
key_terms.بِبَعِيرٍ: with one camel; the stated measure of diyah compensation
key_terms.سِنِّ: tooth; the injured body part under legal consideration
key_terms.قَضَى: ruled or judged; indicating a formal legal judgment
key_terms.يَثَّغِرْ: to shed a tooth naturally; referring to the stage before the tooth falls out

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for the tooth of a child if it has not yet fallen out?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام regarding compensation for the tooth of a child before it has fallen out naturally. It indicates a fixed diyah valuation in cases involving bodily injury to minors.
